card.name: Kabuki
card.era: Early Edo period, c. 1603 (founded by Izumo no Okuni)
card.tagline: Stylized Japanese classical theatre fusing drama, music and dance
card.profile: Kabuki is a classical form of Japanese theatre mixing dramatic performance with traditional dance, known for heavily stylised acting, lavish costumes and elaborate kumadori makeup (Wikipedia). It is thought to have originated in the early Edo period when Izumo no Okuni formed a female dance troupe performing in Kyoto around 1603; after women were banned in 1629 it became all-male, with onnagata specialists playing female roles (Wikipedia). Dance is integral through shosagoto dance pieces, alongside jidaimono history plays and sewamono domestic plays (Artelino). UNESCO proclaimed Kabuki a Masterpiece in 2005 and inscribed it on the Representative List in 2008 (UNESCO).
card.insight: Kabuki's three name-kanji read 'sing, dance and skill,' but the word actually derives from kabuku ('to lean/be out of the ordinary'), reflecting its origins among flamboyant kabukimono outsiders (Wikipedia).
